questions.question: The combination of high levels of which type of fats with low HDL cholesterol or high LDL cholesterol levels can increase the risk of heart attack and stroke?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Triglycerides**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Triglycerides** are a type of fat (lipid) found in your blood, primarily derived from calories consumed that are not immediately used by the body.
 
• High levels of triglycerides in the blood, when combined with low HDL (good cholesterol) or high LDL (bad cholesterol), significantly increase the risk of **heart attack, stroke, and cardiovascular disease.**
 
• Normal triglyceride levels are below **150 mg/dL**; levels above 200 mg/dL are considered high and pose health risks.
 
• Common causes of high triglyceride levels include **obesity, uncontrolled diabetes, excessive alcohol consumption, and high-calorie diets.**
 
• Maintaining a healthy lifestyle, including regular exercise, a balanced diet, and avoiding smoking, can help manage triglyceride levels effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **LDL (Low-Density Lipoprotein):**

 
 
• Known as "bad cholesterol," LDL carries cholesterol to the arteries, where it can form plaques and lead to blockages.
 
• High levels of LDL are a major risk factor for cardiovascular diseases such as heart attack and stroke.
 
• Recommended LDL levels are below 100 mg/dL for optimal heart health.
 
 
 
• **HDL (High-Density Lipoprotein):**
 
 
• Known as "good cholesterol," HDL helps remove excess cholesterol from the bloodstream, transporting it to the liver for excretion.
 
• Higher levels of HDL are associated with reduced risk of heart disease.
 
• Healthy HDL levels are 60 mg/dL or higher.
 
 
 
• **Triglycerides vs Cholesterol:**
 
 
• Triglycerides store unused calories and provide energy, whereas cholesterol is used to build cells and hormones.
 
• Both are lipids, but they serve different functions in the body.
 
 
 
• **Preventive Measures for High Lipid Levels:**
 
 
• Adopt a diet rich in fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and lean proteins while avoiding trans fats and sugary foods.
 
• Engage in regular aerobic exercise to improve lipid profiles and overall heart health.
 
• Limit alcohol intake and quit smoking to reduce triglyceride levels and improve HDL levels.

questions.question: Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyan was introduced by the Government of India in how many states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Six**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyan (GKRA) was launched by the Government of India on **20 June 2020** to boost livelihood opportunities for migrant workers.
 
• This program was implemented in **six states**: Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Odisha, and Jharkhand.
 
• It was initiated as a **125-day campaign** to address the economic distress caused by the reverse migration of workers due to the COVID-19 lockdown.
 
• The program aimed to provide **employment opportunities** in rural areas by utilizing the existing skill sets of migrant workers.
 
• A total of **25 target-driven schemes** from 12 ministries were combined under GKRA, with an allocation of Rs. 50,000 crores.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Targeted States**

 
 
• The six states were chosen based on the large number of returning migrant workers during the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• Bihar had the highest number of districts (32) under the campaign, followed by Uttar Pradesh (31 districts).
 
 
 
• **Focus Areas**
 
 
• The campaign focused on rural infrastructure development such as roads, housing, community centers, and water conservation projects.
 
• It also promoted skill development and self-reliance initiatives under the Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan.
 
 
 
• **Execution and Monitoring**
 
 
• The program was implemented in a coordinated effort by the central and state governments.
 
• It was monitored through a technology-driven platform to ensure transparency and efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Impact and Outcomes**
 
 
• Over 50 crore person-days of employment were generated by the end of the campaign.
 
• The initiative helped stabilize rural economies during the pandemic by creating job opportunities at the local level.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution guarantees equality before the law?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 14**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 14** of the Indian Constitution guarantees **equality before the law** and equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
 
• This article ensures that no person is above the law and emphasizes that laws should be applied uniformly, irrespective of an individual's status.
 
• It is a fundamental right under Part III of the Constitution, promoting the principle of **rule of law**.
 
• The concept of "equality before the law" originates from the British legal system, while "equal protection of the laws" is inspired by the U.S. Constitution.
 
• This article forms the cornerstone of India's commitment to secularism, non-discrimination, and justice in a democratic setup.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Equality before the law:**

 
 
• This concept originates from the rule of law propounded by A.V. Dicey in England.
 
• It means that no individual, regardless of their rank or position, is exempt from the jurisdiction of the ordinary courts.
 
• It prevents any special privileges for individuals or groups under the law.
 
 
 
• **Equal protection of the laws:**
 
 
• This phrase is derived from the 14th Amendment of the U.S. Constitution.
 
• It mandates that individuals in similar circumstances will be treated equally by the law.
 
• However, reasonable classification (not arbitrary) is permitted under this principle.
 
 
 
• **Doctrine of Reasonable Classification:**
 
 
• The state can make laws that apply differently to different groups, provided the classification is reasonable.
 
• It must fulfill two criteria: (i) Classification must be based on intelligible differentia, and (ii) It must have a rational nexus with the object of the law.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights under Part III:**
 
 
• Articles 12–35 of the Indian Constitution enumerate the Fundamental Rights available to citizens.
 
• These rights are enforceable by courts and aim to protect individual freedoms and uphold equality.
 
 
 
• **Exceptions to Article 14:**
 
 
• The President and Governors enjoy certain immunities under Articles 361 and 361A.
 
• Diplomatic immunity is provided to foreign diplomats under international law.

questions.question: A player/team needs to win two consecutive points immediately after '__________' to win the game as per the International Tennis Federation norms.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**deuce**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In tennis, a **deuce** occurs when both players or teams reach a score of 40-all (three points each).
 
• To win the game after a deuce, a player/team must win **two consecutive points**.
 
• The first point won after deuce is called an **advantage**, indicating that the player/team is one point away from winning the game.
 
• If the player/team with the advantage loses the next point, the score returns to **deuce**, and the cycle continues.
 
• This scoring rule ensures that players must earn a decisive two-point lead to win a game after deuce.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Love:**

 
 
• In tennis, **love** refers to a score of zero.
 
• The term is derived from the French word "l'œuf," meaning "egg," which symbolizes zero.
 
 
 
• **Set:**
 
 
• A **set** in tennis consists of games won by a player/team.
 
• A player/team typically needs to win **six games** with a margin of at least two games to win a set.
 
 
 
• **Advantage:**
 
 
• Advantage refers to the point immediately following deuce, where a player/team is one point away from winning the game.
 
• If the player/team with the advantage loses the next point, the score returns to deuce.
 
 
 
• **International Tennis Federation (ITF):**
 
 
• The ITF is the governing body for world tennis, overseeing international tournaments and establishing rules.
 
• It was founded in 1913 and manages key events such as the Davis Cup and Billie Jean King Cup.

questions.question: Which is the most fascinating and unique festival of Assam where the system of quid pro quo comes alive?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Junbeel Mela**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Junbeel Mela is a unique and traditional festival of Assam, which is held every year in the third week of January.
 
• This festival is celebrated by the community of Tiwa tribe and it showcases an ancient reciprocal system.
 
• In Junbeel Mela, people exchange goods through barter system, in which modern currency is not used.
 
• This fair is held in Morigaon district and apart from the Tiwa community, other tribes also participate in it.
 
• Junbeel Mela is not only a platform for trade but also cultural programs, traditional dance and music are organized.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tiwa tribe**

 
 
• The Tiwa tribe is an important tribe of Assam and Meghalaya.
 
• They are also known as "Lalung" and the barter system has a special place in their culture.
 
 
 
• **Barter system **
 
 
• It is an age old trade system in which goods and services are exchanged without currency.
 
• Junbeel Mela is a living example of barter system.
 
 
 
• **Other major festivals of Assam**
 
 
• Bhogali Bihu: Harvest festival.
 
• Ambubachi Mela: A religious fair held at Kamakhya temple.
 
• Rangali Bihu: The biggest and colourful festival of Assam.
 
 
 
• **Name of junbil**
 
 
• The name Junbeel is derived from "jun" (moon) and "beel" (lake), as the fair is held near a crescent-shaped lake.

questions.question: In which of the following Buddhist texts are the rules mentioned for Buddhist monks and nuns?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vinaya Pitaka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Vinaya Pitaka** is one of the three baskets (Tripitaka) of Buddhist scriptures that contains the rules and regulations for monks and nuns within the Buddhist monastic community (Sangha).
 
• The text provides detailed guidance on monastic discipline, including codes of conduct, procedures for resolving disputes, and penalties for violations.
 
• The Vinaya Pitaka is divided into three main parts: **Sutta Vibhanga** (rules for individual monks and nuns), **Khandhaka** (procedural rules for the Sangha), and **Parivara** (a summary and analysis of rules).
 
• It was compiled during the First Buddhist Council held at Rajgir (Rajagriha) shortly after Buddha’s death (parinirvana) to preserve the monastic traditions and teachings.
 
• The Vinaya Pitaka serves as a cornerstone for maintaining the moral and ethical framework of the Buddhist monastic community, ensuring harmony and discipline.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tripitaka (Three Baskets):**

 
 
• The Tripitaka consists of three main texts: Vinaya Pitaka (discipline), Sutta Pitaka (teachings), and Abhidhamma Pitaka (philosophical analysis).
 
• It forms the canonical literature of Theravada Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Sutta Pitaka:**
 
 
• It is a collection of discourses delivered by Buddha and his close disciples.
 
• The Sutta Pitaka focuses on ethical teachings and philosophical concepts.
 
 
 
• **Abhidhamma Pitaka:**
 
 
• This text contains a detailed analysis of Buddhist doctrines and concepts.
 
• It is considered an advanced and systematic elaboration of Buddha's teachings.
 
 
 
• **Role of Monastic Rules:**
 
 
• The rules in the Vinaya Pitaka ensure discipline, ethical conduct, and spiritual growth among monks and nuns.
 
• Adherence to these rules fosters a harmonious and conducive environment for practicing the Dhamma.

questions.question: Which industry type is involved in activities like farming, fishing and forestry?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Primary industry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Primary industry** involves activities that extract natural resources directly from the Earth, such as farming, fishing, forestry, and mining.
 
• These industries are the foundation of the economy, as they provide raw materials for other industries like manufacturing and construction.
 
• Examples include agriculture, where crops are grown; forestry, which involves harvesting wood; and fishing, which supplies seafood for consumption.
 
• Primary industries are typically labor-intensive and depend heavily on natural factors such as climate, soil quality, and water availability.
 
• The role of primary industries is crucial for ensuring food security, raw material supply, and environmental sustainability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manufacturing Industry:**

 
 
• This industry transforms raw materials from primary industries into finished goods or intermediate products.
 
• Examples include automobile production, textile manufacturing, and electronics assembly.
 
• Manufacturing industries are part of the secondary sector of the economy.
 
 
 
• **Service Industry:**
 
 
• Also known as the tertiary sector, this industry provides services rather than goods.
 
• Examples include healthcare, education, finance, and retail.
 
• It relies on human capital and plays a significant role in modern economies.
 
 
 
• **Genetic Industry:**
 
 
• This is a specialized branch of the primary industry focused on genetic modification and breeding.
 
• Examples include fish hatcheries, seed production, and cattle breeding.
 
• It contributes to improving agricultural productivity and biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Primary Industry:**
 
 
• It supports rural livelihoods and provides employment opportunities to millions.
 
• Primary industries are essential for economic growth, especially in developing countries.
 
• They play a key role in conserving natural resources and maintaining ecological balance.

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Sattriya dance form of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sankardev**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sankardev** (1449–1568) was a saint-scholar, poet, playwright, and social-religious reformer from Assam.
 
• He is credited with creating **Sattriya dance**, a classical dance form of India, as part of the **Neo-Vaishnavite movement** in Assam.
 
• Sattriya dance was originally performed in **monastic institutions called Satras**, established by Sankardev to propagate the Vaishnavite philosophy.
 
• The dance form serves as a medium for storytelling and is deeply rooted in **mythological themes and devotional expressions**.
 
• Sattriya was officially recognized as one of the **eight classical dance forms of India** by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sankardev's Neo-Vaishnavism Movement**

 
 
• Sankardev propagated the **Ekasarana Dharma**, a monotheistic religious movement emphasizing devotion to Lord Krishna.
 
• He used art forms like music (Borgeet), dance (Sattriya), and drama (Ankiya Nat) to spread his teachings.
 
• The movement rejected caste discrimination and ritualistic practices, promoting equality and devotion.
 
 
 
• **Satras**
 
 
• Satras are monastic institutions established by Sankardev and his disciples in Assam to promote Vaishnavism.
 
• They function as cultural hubs for the preservation of art, literature, and religious practices.
 
• Sattriya dance evolved and thrived within these institutions.
 
 
 
• **Sattriya Dance Characteristics**
 
 
• The dance combines **expressive hand gestures (mudras), rhythmic footwork, and storytelling**.
 
• It incorporates themes from the **Bhagavata Purana and Krishna-centric mythology**.
 
• Traditionally performed by male monks (Bhakats), it is now practiced by both men and women.
 
 
 
• **Recognition of Sattriya Dance**
 
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi recognized Sattriya as a classical dance form in 2000, bringing it to a national platform.
 
• Efforts are ongoing to preserve this cultural heritage and promote it globally.

questions.question: Muthuswami Dikshitar belonged to which of the following music genres?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carnatic music**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Muthuswami Dikshitar** was one of the **Trinity of Carnatic music composers**, alongside Tyagaraja and Shyama Sastri.
 
• He composed **over 500 kritis**, which are devotional songs in Sanskrit, known for their intricate melodies and lyrical depth.
 
• Dikshitar's compositions often included references to **Hindu deities, temples, and Indian philosophy**, and showcased his mastery of ragas.
 
• He is credited with introducing the **violin** to Carnatic music as an accompanying instrument.
 
• Muthuswami Dikshitar's works are widely regarded as a foundation for **Carnatic classical music** and continue to be performed and studied extensively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carnatic music** is a classical music tradition from South India, characterized by **complex rhythmic patterns, intricate melodic structures, and devotional themes.**
 
• The **Trinity of Carnatic music** (Tyagaraja, Shyama Sastri, and Muthuswami Dikshitar) played a pivotal role in shaping this genre during the late 18th and early 19th centuries.
 
• A **raga** in Carnatic music is a melodic framework composed of specific notes and phrases, serving as the foundation for improvisation and composition.
 
• The ** is one of the most popular forms in Carnatic music, often consisting of three sections: pallavi, anupallavi, and charanam.
 
• Carnatic music is traditionally performed in a concert format**, featuring vocalists and instrumentalists, accompanied by percussion instruments like mridangam and ghatam.

questions.question: In September 2024, wrestlers Vinesh Phogat and Bajrang Punia joined which political party ahead of the Haryana assembly elections?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian National Congress (INC)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Wrestlers **Vinesh Phogat** and **Bajrang Punia** joined the Indian National Congress (INC) in September 2024, ahead of the Haryana assembly elections.
 
• Both athletes are renowned Indian wrestlers and have represented India in various international competitions, including the Olympics.
 
• The decision to join INC comes amidst their ongoing fight for justice regarding allegations of misconduct in the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI).
 
• The INC welcomed their inclusion, emphasizing the party's commitment to supporting athletes and addressing issues related to sports governance.
 
• Haryana, their home state, is known for producing elite athletes, and their entry into politics is seen as a significant move ahead of the assembly elections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian National Congress (INC)**

 
 
• The INC, founded in 1885, is one of India's oldest political parties, playing a pivotal role in the country's independence movement.
 
• It advocates for social justice, secularism, and democratic governance, with a focus on inclusive development.
 
• Notable leaders of INC include Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Indira Gandhi, among others.
 
• INC has historically been influential in shaping India's political and economic policies.
 
 
 
• **Wrestling in India**
 
 
• Wrestling is a traditional and popular sport in India, with significant contributions from Haryana and Punjab.
 
• Indian wrestlers have achieved success in international events like the Olympics, Commonwealth Games, and Asian Games.
 
• Wrestlers like Sushil Kumar, Bajrang Punia, and Vinesh Phogat are celebrated for their achievements.
 
• The sport faces challenges such as governance issues, funding, and support for grassroots development.
 
 
 
• **Haryana Assembly Elections**
 
 
• Haryana's assembly elections are crucial in shaping the state's political landscape and governance.
 
• The state has a history of political competition among parties like INC, BJP, and regional players like INLD.
 
• Key issues include farmer welfare, employment, education, and sports development.
 
• Participation of prominent figures like athletes can influence voter sentiment and election dynamics.

questions.question: Which element was isolated by Marie Curie in 1898 by extracting the remaining radioactive components of pitchblende after removing Uranium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Polonium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Polonium was isolated by Marie Curie in 1898 while studying radioactive elements in pitchblende ore.
 
• The discovery of Polonium marked one of the first instances of isolating a radioactive element beyond Uranium.
 
• Marie Curie named Polonium after her native country, Poland, in recognition of her homeland.
 
• Polonium is a highly radioactive element with the atomic number 84 and belongs to the group of chalcogens.
 
• The isolation of Polonium was pivotal in advancing the understanding of radioactivity and laid the groundwork for further research in nuclear science.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pitchblende:**

 
 
• Pitchblende is a mineral primarily composed of Uraninite, which contains Uranium and other radioactive elements.
 
• It was extensively studied by the Curies during their research on radioactivity.
 
 
 
• **Radioactivity:**
 
 
• Radioactivity refers to the spontaneous emission of particles or radiation from unstable atomic nuclei.
 
• It was first discovered by Henri Becquerel in 1896, which inspired further research by Marie and Pierre Curie.
 
 
 
• **Marie Curie:**
 
 
• Marie Curie was a pioneering physicist and chemist who won two Nobel Prizes in Physics (1903) and Chemistry (1911).
 
• She is renowned for her groundbreaking work on radioactivity and the discovery of Polonium and Radium.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Polonium:**
 
 
• Polonium has been used in antistatic devices and as a heat source in space equipment.
 
• Due to its high radioactivity, it requires careful handling and has limited applications.

questions.question: Delhi signed an MoU with the central government to implement which education scheme in October 2024?

options.text: National Programme for Education of Girls at Elementary Level

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PM-SHRI Scheme**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The PM-SHRI (Pradhan Mantri Schools for Rising India) scheme aims to upgrade and modernize existing schools into model schools aligned with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020.
 
• The initiative covers both central government schools and state government schools, emphasizing the holistic development of students.
 
• These schools will adopt eco-friendly practices, digital learning techniques, and inclusive education frameworks to foster innovation and academic excellence.
 
• The scheme targets providing high-quality education to students while ensuring equitable access to resources and technologies.
 
• As part of the implementation, schools will integrate skill development programs and vocational training to prepare students for future challenges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020:**

 
 
• A comprehensive framework for education reform in India, covering school to higher education.
 
• Focuses on critical thinking, creativity, and holistic learning rather than rote memorization.
 
• Introduces a 5+3+3+4 structure to replace the traditional 10+2 system.
 
• Emphasizes vocational education, multilingualism, and the use of technology in education.
 
 
 
• **Eco-Friendly Practices in Schools:**
 
 
• Includes the use of solar energy, rainwater harvesting, and waste management systems.
 
• Promotes environmental awareness and sustainability among students.
 
• Aligns with the national goals of combating climate change and promoting green initiatives.
 
 
 
• **Digital Learning:**
 
 
• Incorporates smart classrooms, e-content, and AI-based tools for personalized learning.
 
• Bridges the digital divide by providing access to technology in rural and underserved areas.
 
• Supports remote and hybrid learning, especially during crises like the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
 
 
• **Skill Development in Schools:**
 
 
• Includes training in coding, robotics, and vocational skills to align education with industry needs.
 
• Prepares students for entrepreneurship and employment opportunities.
 
• Encourages hands-on learning and innovation through project-based activities.

questions.question: In which year was veteran actor and Bharatanatyam dancer Vyjayanthimala Bali given the Padma Vibhushan award?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2024**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Veteran actor and accomplished Bharatanatyam dancer Vyjayanthimala Bali was conferred the **Padma Vibhushan award in 2024**, recognizing her significant contributions to Indian cinema and classical dance.
 
• The Padma Vibhushan is India’s second-highest civilian award, given for exceptional and distinguished service across various fields.
 
• Vyjayanthimala is celebrated for her groundbreaking performances in Bollywood and her mastery of the classical dance form Bharatanatyam.
 
• Her career spans decades, with iconic roles in movies like "Madhumati," "Devdas," and "Sangam," earning her critical acclaim and numerous accolades.
 
• The Padma Vibhushan award in 2024 highlights her enduring legacy as a cultural icon in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Padma Awards:**

 
 
• The Padma Awards are among the highest civilian honors in India and are announced annually on Republic Day.
 
• They are divided into three categories: Padma Vibhushan (second-highest), Padma Bhushan (third-highest), and Padma Shri (fourth-highest).
 
• The awards are conferred in disciplines such as art, literature, education, sports, medicine, social work, science, public affairs, and more.
 
• The Padma Vibhushan recognizes "exceptional and distinguished service" in any field.
 
 
 
• **Vyjayanthimala's Contributions:**
 
 
• She is a pioneer in seamlessly blending Bharatanatyam into mainstream cinema, elevating the art form’s prominence.
 
• She has been awarded several honors, including multiple Filmfare Awards for her acting prowess.
 
• Beyond films, her Bharatanatyam performances have been showcased globally, earning her accolades as a cultural ambassador.
 
 
 
• **Bharatanatyam:**
 
 
• Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originating in Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, intricate footwork, hand gestures (mudras), and facial expressions.
 
• The dance form often conveys spiritual themes and stories from Hindu mythology.
 
 
 
• **Bollywood Legacy:**
 
 
• Vyjayanthimala is regarded as one of the first female superstars of Indian cinema.
 
• Her work in films like "Amrapali" showcased her dual talents in acting and classical dance.
 
• She paved the way for actresses to take up roles that combined glamour with substance.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the adjudication of interstate water disputes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 262**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 262** of the Indian Constitution provides for the adjudication of disputes or complaints regarding the use, distribution, and control of waters of inter-state rivers and river valleys.
 
• It gives the **Parliament the authority** to make laws for resolving inter-state water disputes.
 
• Parliament has enacted two key laws under this article: **the River Boards Act, 1956**, and **the Inter-State Water Disputes Act, 1956**.
 
• The provision explicitly states that the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court or any other court is barred in matters related to such disputes.
 
• This article ensures that water disputes are settled through designated mechanisms to prevent prolonged legal battles and maintain inter-state harmony.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **River Boards Act, 1956:**

 
 
• This act provides for the establishment of River Boards by the Central Government to advise states on the regulation and development of inter-state rivers and river valleys.
 
• The boards facilitate coordination between states for effective water resources management.
 
 
 
• **Inter-State Water Disputes Act, 1956:**
 
 
• This act empowers the Central Government to set up a tribunal for the adjudication of disputes between states regarding inter-state river waters.
 
• Tribunal decisions are final and binding on the parties involved.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Inter-State Water Disputes:**
 
 
• Some notable disputes include the Cauvery Water Dispute (Karnataka and Tamil Nadu), the Krishna Water Dispute, and the Ravi-Beas Dispute.
 
 
 
• **Federal Principle and Water Disputes:**
 
 
• Water disputes highlight the challenges of federalism in India, as water resources often span multiple states, requiring cooperative governance.

questions.question: Which of the following players has won the Arjuna Award in Badminton in 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lakshya Sen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lakshya Sen, an emerging badminton player from India, received the prestigious **Arjuna Award in 2022** for his outstanding achievements in the sport.
 
• He is one of India's top singles badminton players and has consistently performed well in international tournaments.
 
• In 2022, Lakshya Sen won the **gold medal in men's singles** at the Commonwealth Games held in Birmingham.
 
• He also reached the **finals of the All England Open 2022**, becoming the first Indian male player to do so in over two decades.
 
• The Arjuna Award is conferred to athletes for their excellence in sports and their contributions to promoting the sport in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arjuna Award:**

 
 
• It is one of India's highest sporting honors, instituted in 1961, to recognize outstanding performance in sports.
 
• Recipients of the Arjuna Award receive a bronze statuette of Arjuna, a certificate, ceremonial dress, and a cash prize.
 
• The award encourages athletes to achieve greater excellence in their respective sports disciplines.
 
 
 
• **Lakshya Sen's Career Highlights:**
 
 
• Lakshya Sen is known for his agility, technical skills, and composure on the court.
 
• He is an alumnus of the Prakash Padukone Badminton Academy, where he honed his skills under world-class coaching.
 
• Sen achieved his career-high BWF World Ranking of **6** in 2022.
 
 
 
• **Other Major Achievements in 2022:**
 
 
• India's badminton team, including Lakshya Sen, won the historic **Thomas Cup in 2022**.
 
• He also won the **India Open 2022**, part of the BWF World Tour Super 500 series.
 
 
 
• **Commonwealth Games and Indian Badminton:**
 
 
• Badminton is one of India's strongholds in the Commonwealth Games, with multiple golds in men's and women's singles.
 
• India's consistent performance in badminton at international levels has elevated its stature globally.

questions.question: Which of the following crops saw a significant increase in area and productivity due to the Green Revolution in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wheat and rice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution in India primarily targeted crops like **wheat and rice** to enhance their production and address food shortages.
 
• It began in the mid-1960s with the introduction of **high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds**, improved irrigation techniques, and increased use of fertilizers and pesticides.
 
• **Wheat production** saw a significant boost in states like Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh due to favorable climatic conditions and modern farming methods.
 
• **Rice cultivation** expanded in regions like Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, and West Bengal, ensuring food security in India.
 
• The Green Revolution transformed India from a food-deficient country to a **self-sufficient nation** in grain production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High-Yielding Variety (HYV) Seeds:** These are genetically improved seeds introduced during the Green Revolution to boost crop yield. Examples include varieties of wheat like Sonalika and Kalyan Sona.
 
• **Fertilizers and Pesticides:** The use of chemical fertilizers like urea and pesticides improved soil fertility and protected crops from pests, contributing to higher productivity.
 
• **Irrigation Systems:** Large-scale irrigation projects, including canals, tube wells, and dams, ensured a reliable water supply for agriculture.
 
• **Impact on Economy:** The Green Revolution helped in reducing India's reliance on food imports, boosting rural incomes, and driving economic growth in agricultural regions.
 
• **Criticism:** Despite its success, the Green Revolution faced criticism for environmental damage, groundwater depletion, and unequal benefits across different regions and farmers.

questions.question: Which women's organisation was founded by Sarojini Naidu in 1917?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Women's India Association**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Women's India Association (WIA) was founded by **Sarojini Naidu**, Margaret Cousins, and other prominent women in **1917**.
 
• The WIA aimed to promote **women's rights, education, and social reform** in India during the pre-independence era.
 
• It was one of the earliest organizations that worked towards achieving **gender equality** and improving the status of women in India.
 
• The association also played a crucial role in advocating for **universal suffrage** and equal opportunities for women in all spheres.
 
• Sarojini Naidu, known as the "Nightingale of India," was a key figure in the Indian freedom struggle and contributed significantly to women's empowerment through WIA.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharat Stree Mahamandal:**

 
 
• Founded by **Kamini Roy** in 1910, it was one of the earliest women's organizations in India.
 
• The organization aimed to promote **women's education and social welfare**.
 
 
 
• **National Federation of Indian Women (NFIW):**
 
 
• Established in **1954**, this organization works towards **gender equality** and social justice for women.
 
• NFIW is affiliated with various national and international women's rights movements.
 
 
 
• **All India Women's Conference (AIWC):**
 
 
• Founded in **1927** by Margaret Cousins, AIWC is one of the oldest women's organizations in India.
 
• The organization focuses on **women's education, health, and empowerment**.
 
 
 
• **Sarojini Naidu's Legacy:**
 
 
• She was the first Indian woman to become the **President of the Indian National Congress** in 1925.
 
• She also served as the first woman Governor of an Indian state after independence (**Uttar Pradesh**).

questions.question: Which physiographic zone of Uttarakhand is popularly known as Himadri? This zone comprises the Zaskar and sections of the Great Himalayan ranges.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Northern**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Himadri zone, also known as the Greater Himalayas, is located in the **northernmost physiographic zone** of Uttarakhand.
 
• It consists of prominent mountain ranges such as the **Zaskar Range** and sections of the **Great Himalayan Range**.
 
• This zone includes some of the highest peaks in India, such as **Nanda Devi, Trishul, and Kedarnath**.
 
• The Himadri region is characterized by **perennial snow, glaciers, and high-altitude passes**.
 
• It serves as the origin of major rivers like the **Ganga and Yamuna**, which are fed by glaciers from this zone.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Himadri (Greater Himalayas):**

 
 
• The Himadri is the innermost and highest part of the Himalayan range, extending from Jammu & Kashmir to Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• The average altitude of this range is **above 6,000 meters** (19,700 feet).
 
• It is home to some of the world's highest peaks, including **Mount Everest and Kanchenjunga**.
 
• Geologically, this zone is composed of **crystalline rocks** and ancient rock formations.
 
 
 
• **Physiographic Zones of Uttarakhand:**
 
 
• Uttarakhand consists of **five main physiographic zones**: Himadri, Himachal (Lesser Himalayas), Shivaliks (Outer Himalayas), the Doon Valley, and the Terai-Bhabar region.
 
• Each zone has distinct topographical and climatic characteristics, contributing to the state's diverse geography.
 
 
 
• **Glaciers of the Himadri:**
 
 
• Famous glaciers in this region include the **Gangotri Glacier** (source of the Ganga) and **Yamunotri Glacier** (source of the Yamuna).
 
• Glacial meltwater is critical for the sustenance of rivers and agriculture in the plains of North India.
 
 
 
• **Importance of the Himadri Zone:**
 
 
• The Himadri plays a vital role in **climate regulation** due to its impact on monsoonal patterns and glacial water resources.
 
• It is also significant for **biodiversity conservation**, with several endemic and rare species inhabiting the region.

questions.question: If the government decides to privatise a major public sector industry, what might be an unintended consequence?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Potential monopolistic practices**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Privatisation of major public sector industries can lead to the concentration of ownership and control in a few private entities, increasing the likelihood of monopolistic practices.
 
• Monopolistic behavior may result in price manipulation, reduced competition, and exploitation of consumers due to the absence of sufficient market regulation.
 
• Essential services provided by the industry may become less accessible or unaffordable for economically weaker sections of society.
 
• Government oversight may diminish after privatisation, making it harder to enforce regulations to prevent monopolistic tendencies.
 
• In the absence of adequate checks, the industry may prioritize profit over public welfare, negatively impacting service quality and equitable resource allocation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Privatisation:**

 
 
• Privatisation refers to transferring ownership and management of public sector enterprises to private entities.
 
• Its main objectives include enhancing operational efficiency, reducing fiscal burden, and encouraging private investment.
 
 
 
• **Monopoly:**
 
 
• A monopoly exists when a single entity dominates the market, with little or no competition.
 
• Monopolies can lead to higher prices, reduced innovation, and limited consumer choices.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Oversight:**
 
 
• Regulatory bodies like the Competition Commission of India (CCI) are tasked with ensuring fair practices and curbing monopolistic behavior.
 
• Privatisation may require stronger regulatory frameworks to balance profit motives with public interest.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact:**
 
 
• Privatisation can boost economic growth by attracting private investment and enhancing operational efficiency.
 
• However, unchecked privatisation may lead to negative externalities, such as income inequality and reduced access to essential services.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the National Population Policy 2000 is incorrect?

options.text: Providing free and compulsory schooling up to the age of 14 years
Achieve universal immunization of children against all vaccines
Reducing infant mortality rate to below 15 per 1000 live births

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **National Population Policy (NPP) 2000** was introduced to address the unmet needs of contraception, healthcare infrastructure, and health personnel.
 
• The policy aims to achieve a stable population by **2045**, consistent with sustainable economic growth, social development, and environmental protection.
 
• One of the goals is to reduce **infant mortality rate (IMR)** to below 30 per 1000 live births by 2010, not 15 as mentioned in Option 4.
 
• It promotes **universal immunization** for children, free and compulsory education for children up to age 14, and delayed marriage for girls to reduce fertility rates.
 
• The policy also emphasizes increasing access to reproductive healthcare services and creating awareness about family planning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Infant Mortality Rate (IMR):**

 
 
• IMR refers to the number of infant deaths (under 1 year of age) per 1000 live births in a given year.
 
• According to the NPP 2000, the goal was to reduce IMR to less than 30 by 2010.
 
• Achieving a low IMR is crucial for improving the overall health of a population.
 
 
 
• **Universal Immunization Programme (UIP):**
 
 
• Launched in 1985, UIP is one of the largest health programs globally, targeting vaccine-preventable diseases.
 
• It aims to immunize children against diseases such as polio, tuberculosis, measles, and diphtheria.
 
• UIP aligns with the NPP 2000 objective of universal child vaccination.
 
 
 
• **Free and Compulsory Education:**
 
 
• The policy emphasizes free and compulsory education for children up to 14 years of age as a means to empower them and reduce fertility rates.
 
• This is in line with the Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009.
 
 
 
• **Delayed Marriage for Girls:**
 
 
• NPP 2000 promotes raising the marriage age for girls to 18 or higher to improve maternal and child health.
 
• Delayed marriage helps reduce adolescent pregnancies and ensures better health outcomes for mothers and children.
 
 
 
• **Goals of NPP 2000:**
 
 
• Achieve replacement-level fertility (Total Fertility Rate of 2.1) by 2010.
 
• Reduce maternal mortality ratio (MMR) to below 100 per 100,000 live births by 2010.
 
• Promote contraception and access to reproductive health services for all.
